transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what’s been bothering you or what brings you in today?

Hi, Doctor. Thank you for seeing me. I hope I'm not taking up time someone else might need more... but, um, I guess I'm here because things have just felt a bit... flat lately? 

I mean, I'm still working—I'm a social worker, so I know how important it is to keep up with my obligations, and I'm definitely doing that. I'm fine there. But it's just that the part of me that used to really reach out for people, or enjoy things like my yoga classes, or going to galleries, or even just journaling... it’s gone very quiet. I’m mostly just going through the motions right now. I know that probably sounds a bit silly, or maybe not severe enough to be here, but it's just not like me. Does that make sense? I just want to make sure I'm explaining it right.
How long have you been feeling this way? When did you first notice these changes in your mood or interest in activities?

Well, um... I guess it's been a little while now. Maybe around eight months? 

It started right around the time my husband and I had my older relative move into our apartment. Which, of course, I was happy to do! Family is so important, and I really wanted to help. I don't want to sound like I'm complaining about that at all. It's just... I think since then, that's when I started noticing this shift in how I'm thinking, and how I'm connecting with people, and even just how I'm working. 

I really hope I'm not making too big a deal out of it. It's just an adjustment, I'm sure. Does eight months sound like a normal amount of time to still be adjusting to something like that?
Have you noticed any other changes besides feeling flat and losing interest in things—like changes in your sleep, appetite, energy level, or maybe trouble concentrating or feeling down on yourself?

Um, let me think... no, I don't think so. I mean, I'm sleeping alright, and I'm still eating normally. I definitely don't want to make it sound like I'm falling apart or anything, because I'm really not! 

My energy is... well, it's fine. It's enough to get through the day, and I'm still getting all my case notes done at work, so my concentration must be okay, right? I don't feel bad about myself, exactly, just... muted, I suppose. 

I really hope it's okay that I don't have those other things you mentioned. I know you're trying to get a full picture, and I want to make sure I'm giving you the right answers. I'm trying to be as helpful as I can... does it still make sense for me to be here even if my sleep and appetite are fine?
Can you tell me a bit more about this feeling of being 'muted'—does it feel like you’re not enjoying anything at all anymore, or more like you just don’t care as much as you used to?

Um... that’s a really good question. I’m not entirely sure how to separate the two, to be honest. I mean, I definitely still care. I care so much about my clients, and my husband, and my relative. I really wouldn't want you to think I've just stopped caring about my responsibilities or the people in my life, because I haven't at all! 

I guess it’s more just... I don't feel that little spark from things like I used to? Like, if I think about my yoga class or journaling, I still know it's good for me, but the actual feeling of enjoyment is just sort of... not there. It’s just quiet. Not bad! Just quiet. 

I’m sorry, I don't know if that really answers what you were asking. Is it okay if I’m not completely sure which one it is? I just hope I'm making sense and giving you what you need.
Can you think of a time recently when something used to bring you joy or pleasure—like your yoga class or journaling—and whether you still felt any sense of enjoyment or reward from it?

Um, let me think about that. That's a really good question... I want to make sure I give you a good example. 

I guess... well, I went to my yoga class last Tuesday. I used to really look forward to it, you know? It was my time to unwind and feel centered. And I went! I made sure I went, because I know it's important to keep up with healthy habits, and I definitely don't want to just stop doing things. 

But while I was there... doing the poses and everything... I just felt kind of blank. Like I was going through the motions. I didn't feel that sense of relief or happiness I usually get at the end of a session. It wasn't unpleasant or anything! I wasn't upset. Just... I didn't really feel much of a reward from it, I suppose. 

I hope that's an okay example? I don't want it to sound like I'm giving up on my hobbies or anything, because I'm definitely still trying. Does that sound like the kind of thing you were asking about?
Have you been feeling down or having a sad or empty mood most of the day, even if you aren't sure if it's severe?

Um, no, I wouldn't say I feel sad or down. I mean, I definitely don't want you to think I'm depressed or crying all the time, because I'm really not! 

It's more just that quiet feeling I mentioned... the blankness. But it's not a heavy, sad kind of empty, if that makes sense? I'm still getting up and doing what I need to do, and I'm not sitting around feeling sorry for myself. I try to stay really positive and keep moving forward. 

I just... I wouldn't use the word sad. Is it okay if I say no to that one? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the most accurate picture, and I don't want to accidentally steer you in the wrong direction. Does that sound alright?
Have you found that most of the things you used to enjoy don’t give you any pleasure at all anymore, or do they still feel a little rewarding, even if not as much as before?

Um... I really want to be careful with how I answer this, because I definitely don't want to sound ungrateful or like I'm just completely numb to my life. I think... I think things still feel a little rewarding? Just a little. It's definitely not like there's absolutely zero pleasure at all. 

Like, I still feel a tiny sense of accomplishment when I finish something, just knowing I did something healthy for myself or helped one of my clients. The volume on the joy is just... turned down a lot, I guess. I'd really hate for you to think I've totally lost my appreciation for life, because I'm definitely still trying my best to find the good in my day. 

Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it right for you, I just want to make sure I'm giving you exactly what you need.
Would you say that most of the things you used to enjoy feel completely unrewarding now, or do they still feel somewhat meaningful or pleasurable, even if much less than before?

Um, well... I guess I'd say they still feel somewhat meaningful. I really don't want to make it sound worse than it is. I'm still doing my work, and I still go to the galleries when I can, and I try to journal... 

But I suppose... and I hope this is okay to say, because this is actually what finally brought me in to see you... I just feel like the part of me that used to really reach out for people, and the part that used to actually take joy in all those things... my work, my yoga, all of it... it's just gone very, very quiet. 

I'm mostly just moving through my obligations right now. I'm still doing them! I promise I'm still fulfilling all my responsibilities. It's just... quieter inside. Does that answer your question okay? I just want to be sure I'm giving you the right kind of information.
Would you say that this feeling of things being 'very quiet' and not feeling the same joy in activities has been happening most of the day, nearly every day, for the past several months?

Um, yes, I suppose it has been happening most of the day, nearly every day. I really hope I'm not making it sound like I've just been sitting around doing nothing this whole time, because I haven't! But... yes, this whole change in how I'm thinking, working, and connecting with people... it's been going on for about eight months now. 

It started around the time we took my older relative into our apartment to live with us. I really love them, and I'm so glad we can help, so I definitely don't want to sound like I'm complaining or that it's their fault. It's just... that's when I noticed things getting so quiet for me. I've been trying so hard to just keep up with everything and be a good host and a good worker. 

I hope it's okay that I brought up my relative? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right timeline so you have all the pieces you need. Is eight months the kind of timeframe you were asking about?
